stemMd: A city spends a fixed budget on a park instead of a library. What is the opportunity cost of that choice?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Every euro ever spent by the city

options.label: B
options.textMd: The total value of both projects added together

options.label: C
options.textMd: Zero, because the budget was already approved

options.label: D
options.textMd: The park's area in square metres

options.label: E
options.textMd: The value of the best alternative use forgone

explanationMd: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone when resources are committed to one use. Here it concerns what the city gives up by not funding the library or another next-best use. Approval does not remove scarcity.

distractorRationale.a: Only the best forgone alternative is relevant.
distractorRationale.d: Physical area is not opportunity cost.
distractorRationale.c: Scarcity still requires a choice among alternatives.
distractorRationale.b: This does not identify the alternative sacrificed.
